title: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
description: The definitive restaurant-style Butter Chicken — tender chicken thighs marinated in spiced yoghurt, charred under high heat, then simmered in a velvety tomato-cream-cashew gravy. The secret is the double-cooking method and finishing the sauce with cold butter.

ingredients.name: Raw Cashews
ingredients.preparation_note: soaked in warm water 20 minutes, drained

steps.instruction_text: Combine all marinade ingredients in a large bowl. Add the chicken pieces and mix thoroughly until every piece is well coated. Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or overnight for best results.

Heat a grill pan or heavy skillet over the highest possible heat until smoking. Brush with 1 tablespoon of oil. Working in a single layer (no crowding), cook the chicken pieces for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply charred in spots. The chicken will finish cooking in the sauce — slight undercooking at this stage is fine. Set aside.

In a deep saucepan, melt 30 g of the butter with the remaining oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions with a generous pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 15 to 18 minutes until they are soft, golden, and jammy.

Add the chopped tomatoes and drained cashews to the onions. Stir to combine, then cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes over medium heat, stirring twice, until the tomatoes have completely broken down and the mixture looks thick and saucy.

Transfer the onion-tomato-cashew mixture to a blender. Allow to cool for 5 minutes, then blend on high for 90 seconds until completely silky smooth. Pass the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing hard with a spoon, back into the saucepan. Discard the solids caught in the sieve.

Return the sieved sauce to medium heat. Add the Kashmiri chilli powder, garam masala, and ground cumin. Cook, stirring constantly, for 3 minutes until the spices are fragrant and the sauce deepens in colour.

Pour in the heavy cream and stir to fully incorporate. Nestle the charred chicken pieces into the sauce. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.

Remove the pan from heat. Add the remaining cold butter cubes and stir vigorously in circles — this emulsifies the butter into the sauce, creating the characteristic silky, velvety finish. Stir in the crushed kasuri methi and taste; adjust salt and add the caster sugar if the sauce tastes sharp. Serve immediately with naan or basmati rice.

title: Dal Makhani
description: Slow-cooked black whole urad lentils and kidney beans in a smoky, buttery tomato gravy. The hallmark of this dish is patience — minimum 3 hours of low-and-slow simmering transforms the lentils from firm to meltingly creamy. A Punjabi dhaba staple reimagined for the home kitchen.

ingredients.name: Whole Black Urad Dal (whole black lentils)
ingredients.preparation_note: soaked overnight in cold water, drained

ingredients.name: Unsalted Butter
ingredients.preparation_note: divided — 60 g for tempering, 20 g to finish

ingredients.name: Heavy Cream
ingredients.preparation_note: plus extra to swirl on top for serving

steps.instruction_text: Combine the soaked and drained urad dal and kidney beans in a pressure cooker with 1.5 litres of water and 1 teaspoon of salt. Pressure cook on high for 25 minutes (or 6–7 whistles on a stovetop cooker). The lentils should be completely soft — press one between two fingers and it should mash with no resistance. Do not drain; reserve all the cooking liquid.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pot (Dutch oven or similar) melt 60 g of butter over medium heat. Add the finely diced onions with a good pinch of salt and sauté for 18 to 20 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes, until they are deep golden-brown and jammy. Do not rush this step — the caramelised onions are the flavour backbone.

Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes until the raw smell has completely disappeared. Add the Kashmiri chilli powder and ground coriander; cook for 1 minute until the spices sizzle and bloom in the fat.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes. Stir well, scraping any browned bits from the base of the pot. Cook over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the tomato mixture has thickened, turned a deep brick-red, and the butter visibly separates and pools around the edges.

Add the cooked lentils along with all of their cooking liquid. Stir to combine thoroughly. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat, then reduce to the lowest possible flame. Cook, uncovered, for at least 2 hours, stirring every 20 minutes and lightly mashing some lentils against the pot wall to create a naturally creamy texture. Add a splash of water if the dal becomes too thick.
After 2 hours the dal should be thick, glossy, and creamy. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed kasuri methi. Taste and adjust salt. Simmer for a final 10 minutes.

Remove from heat and stir in the remaining 20 g of cold butter to give the dal a luxurious, restaurant-quality sheen. Serve in warm bowls with a swirl of extra cream on top, accompanied by butter naan or steamed basmati rice.

title: Cacio e Pepe
description: Rome's most minimalist masterpiece — three ingredients (pasta, Pecorino Romano, black pepper) transformed into something transcendent. The entire technique rests on emulsification: using the starchy pasta water and the right temperature to create a sauce that clings to every strand without clumping or turning greasy.

ingredients.name: Pecorino Romano
ingredients.preparation_note: finely grated on a microplane — must be at room temperature

ingredients.name: Parmigiano-Reggiano
ingredients.preparation_note: finely grated, optional but adds depth

ingredients.name: Whole Black Peppercorns
ingredients.preparation_note: freshly coarsely cracked in a mortar — NOT pre-ground

ingredients.name: Fine Sea Salt
ingredients.preparation_note: for pasta water — less than usual since Pecorino is salty

steps.instruction_text: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Salt it lightly — less than you normally would, because Pecorino Romano is intensely salty. Cook the pasta 1 to 2 minutes less than the package directs (you want al dente). Reserve at least 300 ml of pasta cooking water before draining — this starchy water is the heart of the sauce.

While the pasta cooks, toast the cracked black pepper in a large, dry skillet over medium heat for 60 to 90 seconds, swirling constantly, until fragrant. Add 60 ml of the pasta cooking water and let it bubble for 30 seconds — this blooms the pepper flavour into the water.

In a wide bowl, mix the grated Pecorino (and Parmigiano if using) together. Add 2 to 3 tablespoons of hot pasta water and stir vigorously with a fork until you have a thick, smooth paste with no dry pockets. It should look like thick Greek yoghurt. The room temperature cheese is critical — cold cheese will not emulsify.

Transfer the drained pasta directly into the skillet with the pepper water. Toss vigorously over medium-low heat for 60 seconds to coat every strand. Remove the skillet from heat completely — this is the most important step. Let the pasta cool for 30 seconds so it is no longer boiling hot.

Pour the cheese paste over the pasta. Using tongs, toss and fold continuously while adding pasta water one tablespoon at a time. Work quickly — the goal is a silky, cream-like sauce that coats each strand. If the sauce looks grainy or dry, the pan is too hot; add more water. If it looks soupy, keep tossing to reduce. You will use roughly 60 to 100 ml of pasta water in total.
Divide into two warm bowls immediately. Add an extra crack of fresh black pepper over each serving. Eat at once — Cacio e Pepe waits for nobody.

title: Osso Buco alla Milanese
description: Milanese-style braised veal shanks in white wine and gremolata — a Lombardy Sunday classic. The marrow-filled bone is the star: spoon it onto the risotto milanese alongside the braising liquid reduced to a rich, glossy jus. Finished with fresh gremolata (lemon, parsley, garlic) for brightness.

ingredients.name: Cross-cut Veal Shanks
ingredients.preparation_note: 3–4 cm thick, tied with kitchen twine around the circumference

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.preparation_note: minced to a paste — for gremolata

steps.instruction_text: Preheat your oven to 160°C (325°F). Pat the veal shanks completely dry with paper towels — moisture is the enemy of a good sear. Season all sides generously with salt and pepper. Dredge each shank in flour, shaking off every bit of excess.

Heat the olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the shanks without touching each other. Sear for 4 to 5 minutes per side until a deep mahogany crust has formed. Do not move them while searing. Transfer to a plate; set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the butter to the same pot. Once it foams, add the diced onion, celery, and carrot (the soffritto). Season with salt and cook, scraping up the seared bits from the base, for 10 to 12 minutes until the vegetables are soft and starting to colour.

Pour in the white wine. Increase heat to high and let it bubble vigorously for 4 to 5 minutes until reduced by two thirds and the sharp alcohol smell has gone. Add the crushed tomatoes and warm stock. Stir to combine.

Return the seared shanks to the pot, bone side down, ensuring the braising liquid comes at least halfway up the meat. Bring to a gentle simmer, then cover tightly with a lid and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2 hours, turning the shanks gently at the 1-hour mark.
While the osso buco braises, make the gremolata: combine the finely grated lemon zest, minced garlic, and chopped parsley in a small bowl. Stir together and set aside at room temperature.

After 2 hours the meat should be falling-tender and pulling away from the bone. Remove shanks carefully and set on a warm plate. Place the Dutch oven on the stovetop over high heat and reduce the braising liquid for 8 to 10 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon. Taste and adjust seasoning.

Remove the kitchen twine from each shank. Plate each shank over risotto Milanese or creamy polenta. Spoon the reduced braising jus generously over the top. Finish each plate with a generous pinch of gremolata. Serve immediately, reminding guests to scoop the marrow from the bone — it is the cook's privilege.

title: Birria Tacos de Res
description: Jalisco-style braised beef birria served the quesabirria way — corn tortillas dipped in the chile-infused consommé, griddled until crispy with melted Oaxaca cheese and shredded beef inside. Served with the consommé for dunking. An all-day project with a life-changing payoff.

ingredients.name: Beef Chuck Roast
ingredients.preparation_note: cut into 8 cm chunks, excess fat trimmed but not all removed

ingredients.name: Bone-in Beef Short Ribs
ingredients.preparation_note: adds collagen and richness to the consommé

ingredients.name: Dried Guajillo Chiles
ingredients.preparation_note: stems and seeds removed, briefly toasted in a dry pan

ingredients.name: Dried Ancho Chiles
ingredients.preparation_note: stems and seeds removed, briefly toasted

ingredients.name: Chipotle Chiles in Adobo
ingredients.preparation_note: from a can, with 1 tbsp of the adobo sauce

ingredients.name: Roma Tomatoes
ingredients.preparation_note: roasted under a broiler until blistered and charred

ingredients.name: White Onion
ingredients.preparation_note: half charred on comal or dry pan, half reserved raw for serving

ingredients.name: Dried Mexican Oregano
ingredients.preparation_note: Mexican oregano is different from Mediterranean — do not substitute

steps.instruction_text: Toast the guajillo and ancho chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 30 seconds per side, pressing them flat with a spatula, until they puff and become fragrant. Do not let them turn black — that creates bitterness. Transfer immediately to a bowl, cover with boiling water, and soak for 20 minutes until completely soft.

While the chiles soak, char the onion half and dry-roast the garlic cloves in the same dry skillet over high heat, turning occasionally, for 8 to 10 minutes until deeply charred on the outside. Squeeze the softened garlic from their skins. Roast the tomatoes under a broiler for 8 to 10 minutes until blistered and blackened in spots.

Drain the soaked chiles, discarding the soaking liquid. Combine the rehydrated chiles, charred onion, roasted garlic, blistered tomatoes, chipotle chiles and their adobo, cumin, Mexican oregano, cinnamon stick, apple cider vinegar, and 250 ml of the beef stock in a blender. Blend on high for 2 minutes until completely smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing firmly.

Season the beef chunks generously with salt and pepper. Heat a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over high heat with 2 tablespoons of neutral oil until smoking. Sear the beef in a single layer, without crowding, for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deeply browned on all sides. Work in two or three batches. Set seared beef aside.

Pour the chile sauce into the pot over medium heat and cook, stirring constantly, for 5 minutes until darkened and fragrant. Return all the seared beef to the pot. Add the remaining beef stock — the liquid should just cover the meat. Bring to a simmer, then cover tightly, reduce heat to the lowest setting, and braise for 3 to 3.5 hours until the beef is fall-apart tender and shreds effortlessly.

Transfer the braised beef to a cutting board. Shred it finely with two forks, discarding any bones or sinew. Skim the brilliant red fat from the surface of the remaining consommé — reserve this fat separately in a small bowl; it is what you will use to cook the tacos. Taste the consommé and adjust salt. Keep warm.

Heat a comal or flat cast-iron griddle over medium-high heat. Using a pastry brush, paint a tortilla on one side with the reserved red chile fat. Place fat-side down on the hot comal. Immediately add a small pile of Oaxaca cheese strands and a generous spoonful of shredded birria to one half of the tortilla. Fold the tortilla in half over the filling. Cook for 2 minutes until the bottom is crispy and deeply golden, then flip for 1 minute more.

Serve the quesabirria tacos immediately alongside small bowls of the hot consommé for dunking. Garnish with finely diced raw white onion, chopped cilantro, and lime wedges. The ritual is to dunk each taco directly into the consommé before each bite.

title: Street-Style Elotes (Mexican Corn on the Cob)
description: Mexico City's most beloved street food — sweet charred corn on the cob slathered in mayo, rolled in Cotija cheese, dusted with chilli powder and tajín, and finished with lime juice. Done in 25 minutes, impossible to eat gracefully, absolutely worth it.

ingredients.name: Cotija Cheese
ingredients.preparation_note: finely crumbled — substitute with Pecorino or Feta if unavailable

steps.instruction_text: Preheat a grill, grill pan, or barbecue to the highest possible heat. You want proper char marks. Brush the bare corn cobs lightly with a thin coat of oil. Place them directly on the grill grates.

Grill the corn, turning every 2 minutes, for a total of 10 to 12 minutes until the kernels are cooked through, nicely charred in spots, and fragrant. You're looking for colour on at least 3 sides. If a few kernels pop slightly — that's perfect.
Insert a wooden skewer or ice-lolly stick through the base of each corn cob to use as a handle. This is how Mexican street vendors serve it.
While the corn is still piping hot, use a pastry brush or the back of a spoon to slather each cob all over with a generous, thick coat of mayonnaise. Work quickly and cover every kernel.

Immediately roll each mayo-coated corn cob in the crumbled Cotija cheese on a flat plate, pressing lightly so the cheese adheres to every surface. Dust generously with chilli powder and Tajín seasoning. Squeeze lime juice over the top. Scatter with chopped cilantro if using. Serve at once.

title: Spicy Tonkotsu Ramen
description: A full from-scratch tonkotsu ramen — milky white pork bone broth simmered 6 to 8 hours, a soy-mirin tare, spicy toasted sesame paste, and all four canonical toppings: chashu pork belly, marinated soft-boiled eggs (ajitsuke tamago), menma bamboo shoots, and nori. This is a weekend project and an act of love.

ingredients.name: Pork Trotters (pig's feet)
ingredients.preparation_note: halved by butcher, blanched in boiling water 10 min, rinsed

ingredients.name: Yellow Onion
ingredients.preparation_note: halved, charred cut-side down in a dry pan until blackened

ingredients.name: Pork Belly
ingredients.preparation_note: rolled tightly and tied with kitchen twine to form a log — for chashu

ingredients.name: Menma (seasoned bamboo shoots)
ingredients.preparation_note: from a jar or vacuum pack, drained

steps.instruction_text: Blanch the pork trotters and neck bones: submerge in cold water in a large pot, bring to a rolling boil, and cook for 10 minutes. The water will turn grey and foamy. Drain completely, rinse every bone under cold running water, and scrub away any grey residue. Clean the pot too. This step is non-negotiable — it removes blood and impurities that would make the broth taste gamey rather than sweet.

Return the cleaned bones to the pot with 3 litres of cold water, the charred onion, ginger coins, and smashed garlic. Bring to a vigorous, rolling boil over the highest heat. Unlike most broths, tonkotsu is intentionally boiled hard — the turbulent boiling emulsifies the fat and collagen into the water, creating the characteristic opaque, milky-white colour. Cook at a full, aggressive boil for 6 to 8 hours, adding water as needed to keep the bones submerged. The broth should remain white and creamy throughout.

While the broth boils, make the chashu: sear the tied pork belly roll in a heavy pan over high heat for 2 minutes per side until golden. Transfer to a snug pot. Combine the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and 200 ml of water; pour over the pork. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over the lowest heat for 90 minutes, turning every 30 minutes. Remove the pork, cool slightly, then refrigerate. Reserve the braising liquid — this is the base of your tare.

Soft-boil the eggs: lower 6 eggs into boiling water for exactly 6 minutes and 30 seconds, then plunge immediately into an ice bath for 5 minutes. Peel carefully. Combine the reserved chashu braising liquid with enough water to make 300 ml and submerge the peeled eggs. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours (overnight produces a deeper flavour and amber colour).

Make the spicy tare: in a small saucepan over low heat, warm the sesame paste with the remaining soy sauce (20ml), mirin (20ml), and togarashi. Stir until combined into a smooth, paste-like sauce. Taste — it should be salty, nutty, and spicy. Set aside.

Strain the finished tonkotsu broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard the bones. Season with salt. The broth should be creamy-white, thick enough to lightly coat the back of a spoon, and deeply savoury. Keep it at a simmer.
Slice the cold chashu pork into 1 cm rounds. Briefly sear each slice in a hot pan with a little oil until the edges caramelise. Halve the marinated eggs lengthwise.

Cook the fresh ramen noodles per the package direction (typically 1 to 2 minutes in rapidly boiling, unsalted water). Drain well. To assemble each bowl: place 1.5 tablespoons of spicy tare in the base of a warm bowl. Ladle in 350 ml of the hot tonkotsu broth and stir to incorporate the tare. Add a portion of noodles. Top with 2 slices of chashu, one halved marinated egg, a pile of menma, 2 half-sheets of nori standing against the bowl edge, and a generous scattering of sliced spring onion. Serve immediately.

title: Tamagoyaki (Japanese Sweet Rolled Omelette)
description: Japan's elegant multi-layered omelette — thin sheets of dashi-seasoned egg mixture rolled together in a rectangular tamagoyaki pan to create a tender, slightly sweet log with a beautiful golden cross-section. A bento box staple and a test of fine knife skills and pan control.

ingredients.name: Dashi Stock
ingredients.preparation_note: prepared from kombu and katsuobushi, or good-quality instant dashi

ingredients.name: Soy Sauce (light)
ingredients.preparation_note: use a light or white soy for a paler colour

ingredients.name: Neutral Cooking Oil
ingredients.preparation_note: for greasing the pan between layers

ingredients.name: Daikon Radish
ingredients.preparation_note: finely grated, gently squeezed, for serving alongside

steps.instruction_text: In a bowl, whisk the beaten eggs with the dashi, light soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and salt until the sugar is dissolved and the mixture is completely homogeneous. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a pouring jug — this removes the chalazae and produces a smoother, more uniform omelette.

Heat a tamagoyaki pan (rectangular omelette pan) over medium heat. Dip a folded piece of paper towel into the oil and rub it evenly over the pan surface. You want a thin, even coat — not a pool of oil. The pan is ready when a drop of egg mixture sets within 3 seconds.

Pour just enough egg mixture to cover the bottom of the pan in a thin layer (roughly one quarter of the total mixture). Tilt the pan to spread it to the edges. When the egg is about 80% set on top — still slightly wet and glossy — begin rolling: using chopsticks or a spatula, roll the egg layer from the far end toward you to form a loose log. Push the log to the far end of the pan.

Re-oil the exposed pan surface with the paper towel. Pour in another quarter of the egg mixture, lifting the existing log so the fresh egg slides underneath it. This fuses each new layer to the previous one. When this layer is 80% set, roll it around the existing log — rolling away from you. Push the log back to the far end.

Repeat the oiling, pouring, and rolling process with the remaining egg mixture in two more additions — four layers total. The log will grow larger with each addition. Work quickly but confidently; rushing causes tearing. If a layer tears, press it back — it will seal as it cooks.

Transfer the finished tamagoyaki to a bamboo sushi mat (or cling film). Roll it firmly into a cylindrical shape and hold for 2 minutes while it cools — this sets the shape. Unwrap and slice into 2 cm thick rounds. Serve at room temperature alongside grated daikon drizzled with a few drops of soy sauce.

title: Greek Spanakopita
description: The classic Greek spinach and feta pie — layers of shatteringly crisp, butter-brushed phyllo encasing a rich, herbaceous filling of wilted spinach, crumbled feta, ricotta, dill, and eggs. Best made the day before serving so the flavours meld and the base stays crisp.

ingredients.name: Fresh Baby Spinach
ingredients.preparation_note: or 4 x 250g frozen spinach blocks, completely thawed and squeezed bone-dry

ingredients.name: Greek Feta Cheese
ingredients.preparation_note: crumbled — use full-fat feta in brine for best flavour

ingredients.name: Full-Fat Ricotta
ingredients.preparation_note: drained in a sieve for 30 min to remove excess moisture

ingredients.name: Spring Onions (scallions)
ingredients.preparation_note: finely sliced, white and green parts

ingredients.name: Phyllo Pastry Sheets
ingredients.preparation_note: approx 12 sheets — thawed overnight in the fridge if frozen, then 2hrs at room temperature; kept covered with a damp cloth at all times

steps.instruction_text: If using fresh spinach: heat a large dry pan over high heat and wilt the spinach in batches, tossing until collapsed (about 90 seconds per batch). Transfer to a colander and allow to cool. Once cool enough to handle, gather the spinach into a ball and squeeze with both hands as firmly as possible over the sink — you must remove as much water as you can. Insufficient squeezing is the single most common cause of soggy spanakopita. Chop the wrung spinach roughly.

Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté the diced onion for 8 minutes until soft and translucent. Add the spring onions and cook for a further 2 minutes. Remove from heat and allow to cool completely before adding to the filling — warm onion will cook the eggs prematurely.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the squeezed spinach, cooled onion mixture, crumbled feta, drained ricotta, beaten eggs, chopped dill, parsley, nutmeg, and black pepper. Mix thoroughly until well combined. Taste — the feta is salty, so you likely will not need additional salt. Set the filling aside.

Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Brush a 33 x 23 cm baking tray generously with melted butter. Working quickly with one phyllo sheet at a time (keeping the rest covered), lay a sheet in the tray, letting any excess drape over the edges. Brush generously with melted butter. Repeat this process with 5 to 6 phyllo sheets total, creating the bottom crust. Each layer must be buttered.

Spread the spinach and feta filling in an even layer over the buttered phyllo base. Use a spatula to press it into the corners. Fold any overhanging phyllo sheets up and over the filling edges, brushing with butter as you go.

Layer the remaining 5 to 6 phyllo sheets over the filling, buttering each one generously. Once all layers are on, tuck the edges down the sides of the pan to seal. Score the top layers of phyllo (do not cut all the way through) into the portion sizes you plan to serve — this makes cutting easier after baking without shattering the pastry.

Sprinkle a few drops of water on the top surface to prevent the edges from curling. Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until the top is uniformly deep golden brown and the pastry is shatteringly crisp when you tap it. Allow to cool for at least 15 minutes before cutting — this allows the filling to set so it slices cleanly.

title: Shakshuka with Merguez
description: A bold, spiced North African tomato sauce enriched with crumbled merguez lamb sausage and harissa, with eggs poached directly in the simmering sauce until the whites are just set but the yolks remain molten. Made in one pan from start to finish — deeply satisfying brunch or weeknight dinner with crusty bread.

ingredients.name: Merguez Lamb Sausages
ingredients.preparation_note: casings removed, meat crumbled — or substitute spicy Italian sausage

ingredients.name: Rose Harissa Paste
ingredients.preparation_note: adjust to your heat preference — Belazu Rose Harissa is recommended

ingredients.name: Canned Whole Peeled Tomatoes
ingredients.preparation_note: two standard cans — crushed by hand

steps.instruction_text: Heat the olive oil in a large, deep oven-safe skillet or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the crumbled merguez and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, for 5 to 6 minutes until browned and caramelised in spots. The fat that renders from the merguez will flavour the whole dish — do not drain it.

Reduce heat to medium. Add the sliced onion and bell pepper to the pan with the merguez fat. Season with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 to 12 minutes until the vegetables are completely soft, sweet, and starting to catch at the edges.
Add the sliced garlic, harissa paste, ground cumin, and smoked paprika. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes until the spices are fragrant and the harissa has darkened slightly.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes. Stir everything together thoroughly. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, uncovered, for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened, the oil is starting to separate at the edges, and the colour has deepened to a rich brick-red.

Make 6 wells in the sauce using the back of a spoon, spacing them evenly. Crack one egg directly into each well. The key for perfect poached eggs: cover the pan with a tight-fitting lid immediately. Cook over medium-low heat for 5 to 7 minutes — 5 minutes for runny yolks, 7 minutes for partially set yolks. Do not let the sauce boil vigorously or the eggs will turn rubbery.

Remove the lid. Scatter crumbled feta and torn cilantro and parsley over the surface. Drizzle with a thread of extra-virgin olive oil. Serve immediately, directly from the pan, with warm crusty bread or khobez flatbread for scooping.

title: Masala Dosa
description: Crisp, golden-brown fermented rice-and-lentil crepes wrapped around a turmeric-spiced potato filling, served with coconut chutney and sambar.

steps.instruction_text: Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds. Once they splutter, add curry leaves, sliced onion, green chillies, and ginger. Sauté until the onion turns translucent.
Stir in turmeric powder and the boiled potato cubes. Mash lightly, season with salt, and cook for 5 minutes until well combined. Set the filling aside.
Heat a flat griddle over medium-high heat and lightly grease with oil. Pour a ladleful of dosa batter in the centre and spread outward in a thin, even spiral.
Drizzle a little oil around the edges and cook until the base turns golden and crisp, about 2 minutes.
Spoon a line of the potato filling onto one half of the dosa, fold over into a half-moon or roll, and serve immediately with coconut chutney and sambar.

title: Chettinad Chicken Curry
description: A fiery, deeply aromatic Tamil Nadu specialty built on a hand-ground roasted spice blend of black pepper, star anise, and dried red chillies.

steps.instruction_text: Dry roast the red chillies, peppercorns, coriander seeds, fennel seeds, and star anise until fragrant. Cool, then grind with the grated coconut and a splash of water into a smooth paste.
Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry the shallots and curry leaves until golden and softened.
Add the chicken pieces and sear on all sides for 5 minutes. Stir in the chopped tomatoes and cook until they collapse into a thick sauce.
Add the ground spice paste and cook, stirring frequently, for 8 minutes until the raw smell disappears and oil begins to separate at the edges.
Pour in 1.5 cups of water, cover, and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes until the chicken is tender and the gravy has thickened. Finish with a final scatter of curry leaves.

title: Pad Thai
description: The iconic Bangkok street-cart noodle dish — chewy rice noodles tossed in a sweet-sour-salty tamarind sauce with shrimp, egg, and crushed peanuts.

steps.instruction_text: Whisk together the tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar until the sugar dissolves. Set the sauce aside.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the garlic until fragrant, then add the shrimp and tofu and cook until the shrimp turns pink.
Push everything to one side of the wok, crack in the eggs, and scramble briefly before folding into the shrimp mixture.
Add the drained noodles and the tamarind sauce. Toss constantly with tongs for 3 to 4 minutes until the noodles are evenly coated and tender.
Add the bean sprouts and garlic chives and toss for another minute. Plate and top with crushed peanuts and a lime wedge.

title: Green Curry Chicken (Gaeng Keow Wan)
description: A vibrant, herbaceous Thai curry built on a homemade green chilli paste and simmered in rich coconut milk with Thai eggplant and sweet basil.

steps.instruction_text: Scoop the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a hot pot and fry over medium heat until the oil begins to separate.
Add the green curry paste and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply fragrant.
Add the sliced chicken and stir to coat in the paste, cooking until the outside is no longer pink.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, then add the eggplant, fish sauce, palm sugar, and kaffir lime leaves. Simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the eggplant is tender.
Remove from heat and stir in the Thai basil leaves. Garnish with sliced red chillies and serve with jasmine rice.

title: Pho Bo
description: A soul-warming Hanoi beef noodle soup with a clear, fragrant broth simmered for hours with charred ginger, star anise, and cinnamon.

steps.instruction_text: Blanch the beef bones and brisket in boiling water for 5 minutes to remove impurities, then rinse clean under cold water.
Char the onion and ginger directly over a flame or under a broiler until blackened in spots, then peel off the charred skin.
Toast the star anise and cinnamon stick in a dry pot until fragrant. Add the bones, brisket, charred onion, and ginger, then cover with water and bring to a boil.
Reduce to a gentle simmer, skim any foam, and cook uncovered for 3.5 to 4 hours, removing the brisket after 1 hour once tender.
Strain the broth, season with fish sauce and salt to taste. Slice the brisket thinly, place noodles and beef in bowls, and ladle over the hot broth.
Serve with a plate of bean sprouts, Thai basil, and lime wedges for guests to add at the table.

title: Banh Mi Sandwich
description: A crackling-crust baguette layered with pâté, five-spice pork, pickled daikon and carrot, cucumber, and fresh herbs.

steps.instruction_text: Combine the julienned daikon and carrot with the rice vinegar, a pinch of sugar, and salt. Let pickle for at least 20 minutes.
Marinate the sliced pork in five-spice powder and soy sauce for 15 minutes, then sear in a hot pan for 4 to 5 minutes until caramelised and cooked through.
Split the baguettes lengthwise and toast lightly. Spread one side with pâté and the other with mayonnaise.
Layer the pork, pickled daikon and carrot, cucumber slices, and cilantro into each baguette.
Press the sandwich together gently and slice in half to serve.

title: Bibimbap
description: A colourful Korean rice bowl topped with seasoned vegetables, marinated beef, a fried egg, and a spoonful of gochujang.

steps.instruction_text: Marinate the sliced beef in soy sauce and sesame oil for 15 minutes, then stir-fry in a hot pan for 3 to 4 minutes until browned.
Sauté the carrot and mushrooms separately, and season the blanched spinach and bean sprouts each with a little sesame oil, garlic, and salt.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up, keeping the yolks runny.
Divide the warm rice between two bowls. Arrange the beef and each vegetable in its own section on top of the rice.
Top each bowl with a fried egg and a spoonful of gochujang. Mix everything together at the table before eating.

title: Korean Fried Chicken (Yangnyeom)
description: Double-fried chicken wings tossed in a glossy, sweet-and-spicy gochujang glaze for the signature crackling Korean crunch.

steps.instruction_text: Toss the chicken wings in potato starch, shaking off the excess, and fry in 175°C oil for 8 minutes until pale golden.
Remove the wings and let rest for 5 minutes, then fry a second time for 5 to 6 minutes until deep golden and shatteringly crisp.
Meanwhile, combine the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, garlic, and rice vinegar in a saucepan and simmer for 3 minutes until glossy and slightly thickened.
Toss the hot fried wings in the sauce until fully coated.
Transfer to a platter and scatter with toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallions.

title: Mapo Tofu
description: Silky tofu cubes and minced pork in a numbing, fiery Sichuan chilli-bean sauce, finished with a heavy dusting of ground Sichuan peppercorn.

steps.instruction_text: Heat oil in a wok and fry the ground pork until browned and crisp at the edges.
Add the doubanjiang, garlic, and ginger and stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant and the oil turns red.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer. Gently slide in the tofu cubes and simmer for 5 minutes without stirring vigorously to keep them intact.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook until the sauce thickens and clings to the tofu.
Transfer to a serving bowl and finish with a generous dusting of ground Sichuan peppercorn and sliced scallions.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: A classic Sichuan stir-fry of diced chicken, roasted peanuts, and dried chillies in a tangy, savoury-sweet sauce.

steps.instruction_text: Combine soy sauce, black vinegar, sugar, and a splash of water in a small bowl to make the sauce; set aside.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat and fry the dried chillies and Sichuan peppercorns for 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn them.
Add the diced chicken and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until just cooked through and lightly charred at the edges.
Add the garlic and scallions and stir-fry for 1 minute, then pour in the sauce and toss to coat.
Stir in the roasted peanuts just before serving so they stay crunchy.

title: Coq au Vin
description: A rustic Burgundian braise of chicken pieces slowly cooked in red wine with bacon lardons, pearl onions, and mushrooms.

steps.instruction_text: Render the bacon lardons in a heavy pot until crisp, then remove and set aside, leaving the fat behind.
Sear the chicken pieces skin-side down in the bacon fat until deeply browned, about 6 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, sauté the pearl onions and mushrooms until golden. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Return the chicken and bacon to the pot, pour in the red wine and stock, and add the thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer, cover, and braise on low heat for 1 hour until the chicken is fork-tender.

Remove the chicken and vegetables. Whisk the softened butter-flour mixture into the simmering liquid to thicken it into a glossy sauce, then return everything to the pot to warm through before serving.

title: Ratatouille
description: A slow-stewed medley of eggplant, zucchini, bell pepper, and tomato in olive oil and herbes de Provence, from the south of France.

steps.instruction_text: Heat half the olive oil in a large pot and sauté the onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and bell peppers and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the eggplant and remaining oil, cooking until it begins to soften.
Add the zucchini and tomatoes along with the herbes de Provence. Season with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until all the vegetables are tender and the mixture has melded into a thick stew.
Remove from heat, taste and adjust seasoning, and scatter with fresh basil before serving warm or at room temperature.

title: Paella Valenciana
description: The definitive Valencian rice dish, cooked in a wide paella pan with saffron, chicken, rabbit or shrimp, and green beans, prized for its crisp socarrat bottom.

steps.instruction_text: Heat olive oil in a wide paella pan and brown the chicken pieces on all sides. Push to the edges.
Add the green beans to the centre of the pan and sauté for 3 minutes, then stir in the grated tomato and smoked paprika, cooking until the tomato darkens.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute to coat every grain in the sofrito.
Pour in the hot saffron-infused stock and distribute the rice evenly across the pan. Do not stir again from this point.

Simmer uncovered over medium heat for 10 minutes, then reduce heat and cook for a further 8 to 10 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Nestle the shrimp on top for the last 5 minutes to cook through.
Increase heat briefly for the final minute to form the crisp socarrat crust on the bottom, then remove from heat, cover loosely with foil, and rest for 5 minutes before serving with lemon wedges.

title: Patatas Bravas
description: Crispy fried potato cubes served with a smoky, spiced tomato bravas sauce and garlic aioli — a staple of Spanish tapas bars.

steps.instruction_text: Parboil the potato cubes in salted water for 5 minutes until just tender at the edges, then drain thoroughly and pat dry.
Heat the oil to 175°C and fry the potatoes in batches for 8 to 10 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Drain on paper towels and season with salt.
For the bravas sauce, sauté the garlic briefly, then add the tomato passata, smoked paprika, and cayenne. Simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Stir the minced garlic and lemon juice into the mayonnaise to make a quick aioli.
Pile the crispy potatoes on a platter and drizzle generously with both the bravas sauce and the aioli.

title: Chicken Tagine with Preserved Lemon
description: Chicken slowly braised with preserved lemon, green olives, and warming Moroccan spices in the classic conical clay tagine.

steps.instruction_text: Rub the chicken pieces with garlic, ginger, cumin, turmeric, and saffron, and let marinate for at least 20 minutes.
In the base of a tagine or heavy pot, layer the sliced onions, then place the marinated chicken on top.
Add a cup of water, cover, and cook over low heat for 45 minutes, turning the chicken once, until tender.
Add the preserved lemon quarters and green olives, and continue cooking uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Scatter with chopped cilantro and serve directly from the tagine with warm crusty bread or couscous.

title: Moroccan Couscous with Seven Vegetables
description: A generous Friday-tradition stew of seven vegetables simmered in a spiced broth, served heaped over fluffy steamed couscous.

steps.instruction_text: Sauté chopped onion in olive oil in a large stew pot, then add the tomatoes, ras el hanout, turmeric, and soaked chickpeas along with plenty of water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes until the chickpeas begin to soften.
Add the carrots, turnips, and pumpkin and continue simmering for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini and cabbage and cook for a final 15 minutes until all vegetables are tender.
Meanwhile, steam the couscous according to package instructions, fluffing with a fork and a drizzle of olive oil.
Mound the couscous on a large platter, arrange the vegetables and chickpeas on top, and ladle over plenty of the spiced broth.

title: Doro Wat
description: Ethiopia's national dish — chicken slow-simmered in a deeply caramelised onion stew with berbere spice, finished with hard-boiled eggs.

steps.instruction_text: Cook the chopped onions in a dry pot over medium heat, stirring frequently, for 20 minutes until deeply softened and beginning to caramelise — no oil needed at this stage.
Add the niter kibbeh, garlic, and ginger and cook for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere spice and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, then add the chicken stock to loosen the paste into a sauce.
Add the chicken pieces, turning to coat in the sauce, cover, and simmer on low heat for 45 minutes until the chicken is very tender.
Nestle the scored hard-boiled eggs into the stew for the final 10 minutes so they absorb the sauce, then serve hot with injera.

title: Misir Wot (Red Lentil Stew)
description: A rich, brick-red split lentil stew spiced with berbere and slow-cooked onions — a staple of Ethiopian fasting cuisine.

steps.instruction_text: Heat oil in a pot and cook the onion over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, and tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then stir in the berbere spice.
Add the rinsed lentils and 4 cups of water. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils have broken down into a thick, spoonable stew.
Season with salt to taste and serve warm with injera or flatbread.

title: Chicken Shawarma
description: Thinly sliced chicken thighs marinated in a blend of warm spices and yoghurt, then seared until charred at the edges for that signature shawarma flavour.

steps.instruction_text: Combine the yoghurt, garlic, spices, lemon juice, and olive oil in a bowl. Add the sliced chicken and toss to coat thoroughly.
Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or overnight for the deepest flavour.
Heat a large skillet or griddle over high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer for 4 to 5 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Let the chicken rest for 3 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Serve piled into warm flatbread with garlic sauce, pickles, and tomatoes.

title: Fattoush Salad
description: A crunchy Levantine bread salad of crisp romaine, cucumber, radish, and tomato tossed with crispy fried pita and a tangy sumac dressing.

steps.instruction_text: Fry or toast the torn pita pieces until golden brown and crisp. Set aside to cool.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, sumac, and pomegranate molasses to make the dressing.
Combine the romaine, cucumber, tomato, radish, and scallions in a large bowl.
Toss the salad with the dressing just before serving.
Scatter the crispy pita pieces on top and toss once more lightly so they stay crunchy.

title: Lahmacun
description: Thin, crisp Turkish flatbread topped with a spiced minced lamb and pepper mixture, baked until the edges blister.

steps.instruction_text: Combine the ground lamb, diced pepper, tomato, onion, parsley, tomato paste, Aleppo pepper, and cumin in a bowl until evenly mixed.
Roll each ball of dough out into a very thin round, about 3 mm thick.
Spread a thin, even layer of the lamb mixture over each round, right to the edges.
Bake in a very hot oven (250°C) on a preheated baking stone or tray for 7 to 9 minutes until the edges are blistered and the meat is cooked through.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over each lahmacun and roll up to eat, or top with chopped parsley and onion salad.

title: Iskender Kebab
description: Sliced döner-style lamb served over cubed pita, doused in tomato sauce and melted butter, finished with a cooling garlic yoghurt.

steps.instruction_text: Marinate the lamb slices with salt, pepper, and a splash of olive oil for 20 minutes, then sear in a very hot pan in batches for 2 minutes per side until charred at the edges.
Whisk the minced garlic into the yoghurt and set aside to let the flavours meld.
Simmer the tomato passata with a pinch of salt and Aleppo pepper for 8 minutes until slightly reduced.
Toast the cubed pita in a dry pan until lightly crisp, then arrange on plates as a base.
Pile the seared lamb over the pita, spoon over the hot tomato sauce, melt the butter and drizzle over the top, and finish with a generous dollop of garlic yoghurt.

title: Ceviche Clasico
description: Fresh white fish 'cooked' in a punchy lime-and-chilli marinade called leche de tigre, served with sweet potato and toasted corn.

ingredients.name: Fresh White Fish Fillet (sea bass or halibut)

steps.instruction_text: Place the cubed fish in a glass or ceramic bowl (avoid reactive metal) and season lightly with salt.
Pour the fresh lime juice over the fish, add the aji amarillo paste, and toss gently. Let sit for 5 to 8 minutes until the fish turns opaque at the edges.
Fold in the sliced red onion and chopped cilantro just before serving so the onion stays crisp.
Spoon the ceviche and its citrusy juices into chilled bowls.
Serve immediately with slices of boiled sweet potato and a scattering of toasted corn kernels.

title: Lomo Saltado
description: A beloved Peruvian-Chinese fusion stir-fry of soy-marinated beef strips, red onion, and tomato, tossed with crisp French fries.

steps.instruction_text: Season the beef strips with salt and pepper. Heat oil in a wok until smoking hot and sear the beef quickly in batches for 1 to 2 minutes, keeping it rare inside. Set aside.
In the same wok, stir-fry the onion wedges for 1 minute, then add the tomato wedges and aji amarillo paste and cook for another minute.
Return the beef to the wok along with the soy sauce and red wine vinegar, tossing everything together over high heat for 1 minute.
Fold in the cooked French fries at the very last moment so they stay crisp, tossing just to combine.
Serve immediately, scattered with chopped cilantro, alongside steamed white rice.

title: Feijoada
description: Brazil's national dish — a hearty black bean stew loaded with smoked and cured pork cuts, slow-simmered until deeply rich, served with rice and orange slices.

steps.instruction_text: Drain the soaked black beans and place in a large pot with fresh water and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 45 minutes.
In a separate pan, brown the pork belly, sausage, ribs, and bacon in batches until nicely coloured.
Sauté the onion and garlic in the rendered pork fat until soft and fragrant.
Add all the browned meats and the onion mixture to the pot of beans. Simmer uncovered for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beans are creamy and the meats are fall-apart tender.
Mash a ladleful of beans against the side of the pot to thicken the stew, season with salt, and serve hot with rice, sautéed collard greens, and orange slices.

title: Brazilian Cheese Bread (Pão de Queijo)
description: Chewy, cheesy little rolls made from tapioca starch instead of wheat flour, naturally gluten-free and irresistibly gooey inside.

steps.instruction_text: Heat the milk and oil together in a saucepan until just simmering, then pour over the tapioca starch in a large bowl and mix until it forms a shaggy, slightly gluey dough.
Let the dough cool for 10 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until fully incorporated.
Stir in the grated Parmesan and salt until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Roll the dough into golf-ball-sized portions and place on a lined baking tray, spaced well apart.
Bake at 190°C for 20 minutes until puffed and golden with a chewy interior. Serve warm.

title: Jamaican Jerk Chicken
description: Chicken marinated overnight in a fiery, allspice-laden jerk paste with Scotch bonnet peppers, then grilled over smoky charcoal.

steps.instruction_text: Blend the Scotch bonnet peppers, scallions, allspice, thyme, ginger, garlic, brown sugar, soy sauce, and lime juice into a smooth, thick marinade.
Rub the marinade all over the chicken pieces, working it under the skin. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator overnight.
Prepare a charcoal grill for indirect medium heat, ideally with a few soaked pimento or allspice wood chips for authentic smoke.
Grill the chicken over indirect heat for 30 to 35 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked through.
Finish over direct heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side to char the skin before serving with rice and peas.

title: Trinidad Doubles
description: Two pieces of soft, turmeric-fried bara bread sandwiching a spiced curried channa (chickpea) filling — Trinidad's favourite street breakfast.

steps.instruction_text: Mix the flour, turmeric, yeast, and a pinch of salt with warm water into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Sauté garlic and curry powder in oil until fragrant, then add the chickpeas, cumin, Scotch bonnet, and enough water to cover. Simmer for 15 minutes, mashing some of the chickpeas to thicken.
Divide the risen dough into small balls and flatten each into a thin round disc.
Fry each disc in hot oil for about 1 minute per side until puffed and golden.
Sandwich a generous spoonful of the curried channa between two bara and serve immediately with tamarind or pepper sauce.

title: Fried Chicken with Buttermilk Biscuits
description: Buttermilk-brined chicken fried to a shatteringly crisp crust, served alongside warm, flaky homemade biscuits.

steps.instruction_text: Marinate the chicken pieces in buttermilk and hot sauce for at least 2 hours, or overnight in the refrigerator.
Combine the flour and paprika with a generous amount of salt and pepper. Dredge the marinated chicken pieces thoroughly, pressing the coating on.
Fry the chicken in 175°C oil for 12 to 15 minutes, turning occasionally, until deeply golden and cooked through. Drain on a wire rack.
For the biscuits, cut the cold butter into the flour and baking powder until pea-sized crumbs form, then fold in the buttermilk just until combined.
Pat the dough out, cut into rounds, and bake at 220°C for 12 to 15 minutes until risen and golden on top. Serve warm alongside the fried chicken.

title: Shrimp and Grits
description: Creamy, cheesy stone-ground grits topped with garlicky shrimp sautéed in a smoky bacon and paprika butter sauce.

steps.instruction_text: Bring the milk and 2 cups of water to a boil, whisk in the grits, and reduce to a simmer. Cook, stirring frequently, for 20 minutes until thick and creamy.
Stir the grated cheddar into the cooked grits until melted and smooth. Season with salt and keep warm.
Cook the diced bacon in a skillet until crisp, then remove and set aside, leaving the fat in the pan.
Sauté the garlic in the bacon fat for 30 seconds, add the shrimp and smoked paprika, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the shrimp turn pink.
Stir the crispy bacon back in with a squeeze of lemon juice, then spoon the shrimp over bowls of the warm cheesy grits and top with sliced scallions.

title: Käsespätzle
description: Soft, hand-cut egg noodles layered with melted mountain cheese and topped with a mountain of deeply caramelised onions.

steps.instruction_text: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk, and a pinch of salt into a thick, elastic batter. Let rest for 15 minutes.
Melt the butter in a wide pan and cook the sliced onions over low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelised.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Press the batter through a spätzle press or colander directly into the boiling water, cooking in batches until the spätzle float, about 2 minutes.
Drain the spätzle and layer in a warm dish alternating with the grated Gruyère and Emmental, allowing the residual heat to melt the cheese between layers.
Top with the caramelised onions and a scattering of fresh chives before serving.

title: Schweinshaxe (Pork Knuckle)
description: A Bavarian beer-hall classic — a whole pork knuckle slow-roasted until the meat is fall-apart tender and the skin turns into deep, crackling shards.

steps.instruction_text: Score the skin of the pork knuckle in a diamond pattern and rub generously with salt and caraway seeds.
Place the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic in a roasting pan as a bed, and set the knuckle on top. Pour in the beer.
Roast at 160°C, covered loosely with foil, for 2 hours, basting occasionally with the pan juices.
Remove the foil, increase the oven to 220°C, and roast for a further 30 to 40 minutes until the skin is deeply crackled and blistered.
Rest for 10 minutes before carving, and serve with the pan juices, sauerkraut, and a soft pretzel or potato dumplings.

title: Chicken Adobo
description: The Philippines' beloved braise — chicken simmered in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, and bay leaf until deeply savoury and tender.

steps.instruction_text: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay leaves, and peppercorns in a pot. Do not stir yet — let it marinate for 15 minutes.
Bring the pot to a boil without stirring, then reduce to a simmer and cook uncovered for 20 minutes.
Turn the chicken pieces, add the brown sugar if using, and continue simmering for another 10 to 15 minutes until the sauce has reduced and thickened.
Optionally, transfer the chicken to a hot pan and sear briefly to crisp the skin, then return to the sauce to glaze.
Serve hot over steamed white rice, spooning the rich sauce generously over the top.

title: Pork Sinigang
description: A comforting Filipino sour soup, its distinctive tang built from tamarind, loaded with pork ribs and vegetables.

ingredients.name: Tamarind Soup Base or Fresh Tamarind

steps.instruction_text: Place the pork ribs, tomato, and onion in a pot with 8 cups of water. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, and simmer for 30 minutes until the pork is tender.
Stir in the tamarind soup base until fully dissolved, then taste and adjust the sourness with more if desired.
Add the daikon and green beans and simmer for 8 minutes until just tender.
Season with fish sauce, add the green chillies, and simmer for 2 more minutes.
Stir in the water spinach just before serving, cooking only until wilted, and serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Beef Rendang
description: A West Sumatran dry beef curry, slow-simmered in coconut milk and a fragrant spice paste for hours until the sauce reduces to a deeply caramelised, almost dry coating.

steps.instruction_text: Blend the shallots, garlic, soaked chillies, and galangal into a smooth spice paste.
Fry the spice paste in a heavy pot until deeply fragrant and the oil begins to separate, about 8 minutes.
Add the beef chunks and stir to coat evenly in the paste, browning lightly on all sides.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, turmeric leaf, and palm sugar. Bring to a boil, then reduce to the lowest simmer.
Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 2 to 2.5 hours until the sauce has reduced dramatically and turns dark brown, clinging thickly to the tender beef.
Continue cooking for the final 20 minutes over low heat, stirring more frequently, until the rendang is almost dry with a deeply caramelised finish.

title: Nasi Goreng
description: Indonesia's beloved fried rice, stir-fried with sweet soy sauce, shrimp paste, and chilli, traditionally topped with a fried egg.

steps.instruction_text: Heat oil in a wok and fry the shallots, garlic, and chillies until fragrant and softened.
Add the diced chicken or shrimp if using, and stir-fry until cooked through.
Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps, and stir-fry over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in the sweet soy sauce and shrimp paste, tossing until every grain is evenly coloured and coated.
Fry the eggs separately sunny-side up, then plate the fried rice topped with a fried egg and cucumber slices.

title: Laksa
description: A rich, coconut-based curry noodle soup layered with shrimp, tofu puffs, and bean sprouts over rice vermicelli.

steps.instruction_text: Fry the laksa paste in a pot with a little oil for 5 minutes until deeply fragrant and the oil separates.
Pour in the stock and coconut milk, stirring to combine, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the tofu puffs and simmer for 10 minutes to let them absorb the broth.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until just pink.
Divide the soaked noodles and bean sprouts among bowls, ladle over the hot laksa broth, and top each bowl with a halved hard-boiled egg and laksa leaf.

title: Satay Ayam
description: Skewered marinated chicken grilled over charcoal and served with a rich, spiced peanut dipping sauce.

steps.instruction_text: Combine the turmeric, ground coriander, lemongrass, and palm sugar, and rub over the chicken strips. Marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Thread the marinated chicken onto skewers.
Blend the roasted peanuts, chillies, coconut milk, and tamarind paste into a thick, smooth sauce, thinning with a little water if needed and simmering for 5 minutes.
Grill the skewers over hot charcoal or a grill pan for 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Serve the satay hot with the warm peanut sauce, sliced cucumber, and compressed rice cakes.

title: Jollof Rice
description: West Africa's smoky, tomato-based party rice, simmered slowly until every grain is infused with deep, spiced flavour.

steps.instruction_text: Blend the tomatoes, red bell pepper, Scotch bonnet, and one onion into a smooth purée.
Fry the second onion, diced, in oil until softened, then add the tomato paste and fry for 5 minutes to remove the raw taste.
Pour in the blended tomato purée and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce reduces and darkens.
Stir in the curry powder, bay leaves, and chicken stock, then add the washed rice, stirring to combine.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 25 to 30 minutes without lifting the lid, until the rice is tender and infused with the smoky tomato flavour, then fluff with a fork.

title: Egusi Soup
description: A hearty Nigerian soup thickened with ground melon seeds, packed with leafy greens, and enriched with palm oil and assorted meats.

steps.instruction_text: Simmer the beef chunks with the onion and a pinch of salt until tender, about 25 minutes, reserving the cooking broth.
Heat the palm oil in a pot and fry a little chopped onion until fragrant.
Mix the ground egusi with a little water to form a thick paste, then spoon dollops into the hot oil and let them fry undisturbed for 5 minutes to form soft clumps.
Break up the egusi clumps and stir in the reserved beef broth, Scotch bonnet, and ground crayfish. Add the beef and stockfish and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the chopped spinach or bitter leaf and simmer for a final 5 minutes until wilted and the soup is thick. Serve with pounded yam or fufu.

title: Tahdig with Saffron Chicken
description: Fluffy saffron basmati rice with a golden, crackling crust of tahdig on the bottom, served alongside saffron-marinated roast chicken.

steps.instruction_text: Marinate the chicken thighs in grated onion, half the saffron water, and lemon juice for at least 30 minutes, then roast at 200°C for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Parboil the soaked rice in well-salted water for 6 to 7 minutes until still firm at the core, then drain.
Mix a ladleful of the parboiled rice with yoghurt and the remaining saffron water. Melt butter in a nonstick pot and spread this mixture evenly across the bottom to form the tahdig base.
Mound the remaining rice on top in a pyramid shape, poke a few holes through with the handle of a spoon, and drizzle with melted butter.
Cover with a cloth-wrapped lid and steam over low heat for 45 minutes until the tahdig is golden and crisp. Invert onto a platter to reveal the crust and serve with the saffron chicken.

title: Fesenjan
description: A luxurious Persian stew of chicken simmered in a deeply flavoured sauce of ground walnuts and tart pomegranate molasses.

steps.instruction_text: Toast the ground walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to let them burn.
Sauté the chopped onion in oil until golden, then add the chicken thighs and brown lightly on both sides.
Add the toasted walnuts and chicken stock, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook on low heat for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent the walnuts from sticking to the bottom.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses and sugar, then continue simmering uncovered for a further 30 minutes until the sauce turns a deep mahogany colour and thickens.
Taste and balance the sweet-tart flavour with more molasses or sugar as needed, then serve over steamed basmati rice.

title: Beef Stroganoff
description: Tender strips of beef and mushrooms in a velvety sour cream and mustard sauce, traditionally served over egg noodles.

steps.instruction_text: Season the beef strips generously and sear in a hot pan in batches for 1 to 2 minutes until browned but still pink inside. Remove and set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the onion and mushrooms until golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the beef stock and Dijon mustard, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in the sour cream, mixing until smooth. Return the beef and any resting juices to the pan and warm through gently without boiling.
Serve immediately over freshly cooked egg noodles, garnished with chopped parsley.

title: Borscht
description: A vibrant magenta beet soup with cabbage and root vegetables, traditionally finished with a swirl of sour cream and fresh dill.

steps.instruction_text: Sauté the onion, carrot, and grated beetroot in a large pot with a little oil for 10 minutes until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then pour in the stock and bring to a boil.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until nearly tender.
Add the shredded cabbage and continue simmering for 15 to 20 minutes until all the vegetables are fully tender and the broth is deep ruby red.
Season with salt, pepper, and a splash of vinegar for brightness, then ladle into bowls and top with a dollop of sour cream and fresh dill.

title: Shepherd's Pie
description: Slow-cooked minced lamb in a rich gravy with peas and carrots, topped with buttery mashed potato and baked until golden.

steps.instruction_text: Boil the potatoes until fork-tender, then mash thoroughly with the butter and milk until smooth. Season with salt and set aside.
Brown the ground lamb in a large pan, breaking it up with a spoon, then add the onion and carrot and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, and beef stock. Simmer for 15 minutes until thickened, then fold in the frozen peas.
Spread the lamb filling in an even layer in a baking dish, then top with the mashed potato, spreading to the edges and roughing up the surface with a fork.
Bake at 200°C for 20 to 25 minutes until the top is golden brown and the filling is bubbling at the edges.

title: Fish and Chips
description: Flaky white fish in a light, crisp beer batter, served with thick-cut chips and a sprinkle of malt vinegar.

steps.instruction_text: Cut the potatoes into thick chips and rinse in cold water to remove excess starch, then pat dry.
Fry the chips in 150°C oil for 6 to 7 minutes until soft but not coloured, then drain and set aside.
Whisk the flour and baking powder with the cold beer until just combined into a light, slightly lumpy batter.
Dip the fish fillets in the batter and fry in 190°C oil for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and crisp.
Increase the oil to 190°C and fry the par-cooked chips a second time for 2 to 3 minutes until golden and crisp. Serve everything together with malt vinegar.

title: Shrimp Étouffée
description: A rich Louisiana stew built on a dark roux, the 'holy trinity' of onion, celery, and bell pepper, and plump Gulf shrimp.

steps.instruction_text: Whisk the flour into the hot oil in a heavy pot and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 12 minutes until the roux turns a deep peanut-butter brown.
Add the onion, celery, and bell pepper to the roux and cook for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the garlic and Cajun seasoning, then gradually whisk in the stock to avoid lumps. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens to a gravy-like consistency.
Add the shrimp and cook for 5 minutes until just pink and cooked through. Serve over steamed white rice, garnished with sliced scallions.

title: Gumbo
description: A hearty Louisiana stew combining a dark roux, andouille sausage, chicken, and shrimp with okra, deeply seasoned with Cajun spice.

steps.instruction_text: Cook the flour and oil together in a heavy pot over medium heat, stirring constantly for 20 to 25 minutes, until the roux reaches a dark chocolate-brown colour.
Add the onion, celery, and bell pepper to the hot roux and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until softened.
Add the sausage and chicken and cook for 5 minutes to brown lightly, then gradually whisk in the chicken stock.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook uncovered for 45 minutes, skimming occasionally.
Add the okra and simmer for a further 20 minutes until the gumbo thickens.
Add the shrimp in the final 5 minutes of cooking, just until pink. Serve ladled over a scoop of white rice.

title: Asado-Style Grilled Short Ribs
description: Bone-in short ribs slow-grilled over wood coals until deeply smoky and tender, served with a bright, herby chimichurri sauce.

ingredients.name: Bone-in Beef Short Ribs (tira de asado)

steps.instruction_text: Season the short ribs generously with coarse salt on both sides and let come to room temperature for 20 minutes.
Combine the parsley, garlic, red wine vinegar, olive oil, oregano, and red pepper flakes in a bowl to make the chimichurri. Let sit for at least 15 minutes so the flavours meld.
Prepare a grill or wood fire for low, indirect heat. Place the ribs bone-side down and cook slowly for about 1.5 hours, turning occasionally.
In the final 10 minutes, move the ribs over direct heat to develop a deep crust on both sides.
Rest the ribs for 5 minutes, then slice between the bones and serve with the chimichurri spooned generously on top.

title: Empanadas de Carne
description: Golden hand pies filled with a savoury beef, onion, and hard-boiled egg mixture seasoned with cumin and paprika.

steps.instruction_text: Sauté the diced onion in oil over low heat for 15 minutes until very soft and sweet, without browning.
Add the ground beef, cumin, and smoked paprika, and cook, breaking up the meat, until browned. Let the mixture cool completely.
Stir the chopped hard-boiled egg and green olives into the cooled beef mixture.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each dough disc, fold over into a half-moon, and crimp the edges firmly to seal, using a repeeting fold or fork press.
Brush each empanada with egg wash and bake at 200°C for 20 to 22 minutes until golden brown.
